title: Accelerate builds by unifying base images and enabling remote cache warmup
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem:
Our current CI pipelines suffer from long cold-start times and duplicated work across services. Image layers are inconsistent between repos, remote cache is not reliably used, and lint/toolchain versions diverge. Median CI job runtime across core services is ~16 minutes; cold caches spike to 30+ minutes. This slows PR feedback loops and blocks feature velocity.

Goal:
1) Standardize and slim base images (runtime-only variants) across the monorepo to remove duplicate layers and reduce layer churn.
2) Integrate a secure remote build cache (S3-backed cache with signed access) and a warmup step so runners get a high cache hit-rate on PRs.
3) Pin and upgrade the JS/Go/Python toolchains and linting configs to a single supported matrix to reduce flakiness.
4) Update Dockerfile patterns and CI workflows so images are reusable as hermetic build toolchains.

Success metrics:
- Reduce median CI job duration from 16m -> <=10m for core pipelines.
- Cold-cache builds <15m for 90th percentile after warmup step.
- Cache hit rate >=75% within 2 minutes of pipeline start.

Scope / high-level plan:
- Create new base-image repo and publish versioned artifacts (slim-debian:2025.02).
- Replace per-repo Dockerfiles with a shared multi-stage pattern referencing the base image.
- Add a remote cache service (S3 + signed tokens) + helper in CI to warm an ephemeral runner via parallel prefetch.
- Migrate lint/toolchain via dockerized toolchain image (node 20.x, go 1.21, python 3.11) and update CI steps to use the image rather than ephemeral installs.
- Add post-merge rollout monitoring dashboards for build times and cache hit rates.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Introducing remote cache requires KMS permissions and longer initial infra work (security gating).
- Consolidating base images may temporarily increase PR churn for repos that expect different runtime libs; mitigation: phased opt-in with compatibility shim layer.
- Upgrading linters may surface a large number of new failures; mitigation: autofix pass + staged enforcement (warnings -> errors).
acceptance_criteria: All core services use the shared base image in their Dockerfiles or have documented exemption
Remote build cache integrated into primary CI (GitHub Actions) and cache metrics visible in console
Median CI job duration for core pipelines is <=10 minutes (measured over 1 week)
Prebuilt toolchain image available and used by lint/test steps (node/go/python pinned)
Documentation and upgrade guide published in Confluence with rollback steps

2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Spike completed. Proof-of-concept remote cache implemented using S3 + signed URLs. Observed 62% cache hit rate on warm runners. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/742
2025-02-22 - Dev Lead (Ava Martinez): Approved phased rollout. Action: start with four high-traffic repos, run canary for two weeks before org-wide migration.

2025-02-28 - Liam Chen: Reworked Dockerfile templates to use multi-stage pattern and moved common apt installs to base image. Draft PRs opened across services: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-a/pull/1286, https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-b/pull/909
2025-03-02 - QA (Noah Brooks): Noted flaky tests when using node 20. Added task to pin npm ci flags and set CI_MEM to limit memory usage. We should run a compatibility matrix in next cycle.
2025-03-03 - Liam Chen: Warmup step added to GH Actions. Early numbers: median job time down to 11m for canary repos. Tracking outstanding lint failures to be auto-fixed via codemods.
review_notes: Design review 2025-02-16: Security expressed need for short-lived credentials for cache access. Action: integrate AWS STS role assumption and KMS-envelope encryption.
Engineering review 2025-02-25: Recommended creating a lightweight compatibility shim layer for repos that need extra OS packages (ex: image-processing service).
PM review 2025-02-27: Confirmed rollout gate: cache hit rate >=70% and median job time <=11m for 3 out of 4 canaries.
